title: Shannon v. Shannon, S-25-546 (Neb. 2026)

reading.body:
The record here does not describe a deployed AI system at all. It is a state supreme court case citation, reported by two legal sources on the same day, and the underlying article text is not readable. Nothing in the available facts identifies a model, a product, a deployment, or a failure mode, so no AI incident can be characterised from this entry.

What the entry does show is a gap in the database itself. An incident record was created with a title, two court-reporting URLs, and no readable text, and the summary field states plainly that no summary can be provided. That is a data quality failure at the point of ingestion, not a failure of any AI system in the world.

It is not established what the case concerned, whether any AI system was involved, or why the record was created. The two reports are court documents, and a filing or a citation is not a finding about technology.

summary: The article text is not readable, so no summary can be provided.
